institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Other people's recommendations, location (south, different continent, far away)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Reasonably easy, there were many emails & I really had to keep up with sorting important vs. non-important stuff and often had to ask my colleagues for information. But in the end, it worked out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student dorm on campus, Student dorm slightly further away from campus (but still campus offered)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: On-campus prepared food, a non-equipped kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Yes, definitely.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: More kitchen utensils would have been great but it did work out like that.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bit confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can choose between many courses and are relatively free in doing so. That was nice. However, the wait times are not really convenient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Profs & online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the classes I wanted to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try as many courses as you can in the course registration period, KU did accept all my proposed courses and I really could choose according to the teacher & topic and not only the title and description.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Took 2 undergrad, and 2 grad courses. Grad courses were easier and less competitive (because grades are not curved), would definitely recommend this if you're optimizing for an easy semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less group work, more competitive, way more assignment work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Game Theory
Public Policy & Ethics
Microeconomics & Public Policy
Peoples and Cultures of South East Asia

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Applied Game Theory, great prof
Peoples and Cultures of South East Asia, because you're there and it's nice to learn something about the culture of your host country.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries were way more expensive than I anticipated

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive than expected, sports facilities on campus were free

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: amazing sports facilities!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything! Very, very broad and comprehensive

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Everything sports, hikes, swims, etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go traveling, to Korea, Japan, Taiwan, South East Asia, and go hiking!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Good, you're still in an international bubble :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use Tinder to connect to locals (you can just use it as "I'm looking for friends"), elevated my stay very much!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are a bit less friendly than in Denmark, everything is extremely fast-paced.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, Music, Hikes, Family-based values

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't judge
Spend your weekends seeing things (city or nature), even the uni is stressful. You can always study but you can only be in Hong Kong once
Eat Indian Food

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read a lot about the culture, and ask other people who've been there what to do, talk to locals, they know better

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My connections with people outside the exchange program (local students, Ph.D. students, etc.)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
